answer: A dawn ceremony stops one operator running many identities at once. At dawn, all applicants answer prompts in one window, so one mind cannot be reused across seats. Answers are clustered; a violet flag marks close matches, and the flagged cluster loses its bond. Each seat posts 80 credits; the k-th fake needs its own 80 plus a distinct live answer, so 1,000 fakes risk 80,000 credits, no bulk discount. Named failure, stand-in staffing: one stand-in covers only one seat at dawn. Flagged bonds go on the timber board; honest applicants answer once, pay once, keep the bond.
